Non-brand paid search spend in Q3 2025 was $5,404,832.95. That covers the weeks whose Monday falls between 2025-07-01 and 2025-09-30.

{"answer": 5404832.95, "refused": false}

Brand-role channels received about 19.15% of 2025 paid media spend.

- Brand spend was $8,250,000.
- Total paid spend was $43,075,000. That is performance at $32,950,000, brand at $8,250,000 and events at $1,875,000.
- 8,250,000 ÷ 43,075,000 ≈ 19.15%.

I counted weeks whose Monday falls in 2025, and I treated all nine paid channels, including events, as paid media.

{"answer": 19.15, "refused": false}

Paid Search Non-Brand had the highest paid spend in 2023, at about $8.45M. Paid Search Brand was next at about $6.0M.

Connected TV spend in the Columbus region in 2024 was $478,223.11. This counts weeks whose Monday falls in 2024, so the week of 2024-01-01 is in and the week of 2024-12-30 is out.

{"answer": 478223.11, "refused": false}

Meta had 112,044,535 impressions in the first half of 2025. That covers the weeks whose Monday falls between 2025-01-01 and 2025-06-30.

{"answer": 112044535, "refused": false}

LinkedIn's 2024 click-through rate was about 0.60%. That is 267,612 clicks divided by 44,409,398 impressions, which comes to 0.603%.

{"answer": 0.6, "refused": false}

Non-brand paid search had a CPC of about $9.00 in Q2 2024. That is $3,653,028.57 of spend over 406,086 clicks. I counted weeks whose Monday falls between 2024-04-01 and 2024-06-30.

{"answer": 8.9957, "refused": false}

{"answer": 10.22, "refused": false}

Meta reported 165,300 conversions on its own platform in 2025. This is the platform-reported figure, which counts every conversion Meta claims it touched. It overlaps with other channels and is higher than the number of real CRM leads.

{"answer": 165300, "refused": false}

The 2024 win rate was 31.73%. That is 27,658 closed-won deals out of 87,155 closed deals, which is 27,658 won plus 59,497 lost.

{"answer": 31.73, "refused": false}

Meta's MQL rate for 2024 was 45.55%. This is MQLs divided by leads for leads sourced from Meta, using the CRM's last-touch source. It is an event-week rate, not a cohort rate.

Chicago had the most closed-won deals in 2024, with 5,348. Minneapolis-St. Paul was next with 3,167.

Last-touch ROAS for affiliates in 2025 was about 2.21. The data has one combined "Affiliates and Partners" channel, so that figure covers affiliates and partners together, not affiliates alone. The latest 2025 weeks also undercount closed deals because recent leads haven't had time to close, so the true figure may be a little higher.

{"answer": 2.2139, "refused": false}

{"answer": 66.41, "refused": false}

{"answer": 2.96, "refused": false}

Webinars had the lowest last-touch CPA among paid channels in 2025, at about $1,318.57 per closed-won deal. That is $1.875M of spend over 1,422 deals. Paid Search Brand was next at about $1,354.94. Connected TV had no last-touch closed-won deals, so I left it out as the question requires.

{"answer": "Webinars", "refused": false}

Combined last-touch CPL for Paid Search Brand and Non-Brand in 2024 was about $91.65. That is total spend of $19,224,999.92 divided by 209,773 leads.

| Channel | Spend | Leads | CPL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Brand | $13,049,999.93 | 95,846 | $136.16 |
| Brand | $6,174,999.99 | 113,927 | $54.20 |

I pooled spend and leads across the two channels rather than averaging the two CPLs.

I can't answer this one. Fernhook's governed metrics don't include customer churn or retention, or any count of customers lost or renewed. The closest metrics are closed-lost deals and win rate. Those measure sales opportunities that were lost, not existing customers who left. Using them as a stand-in for churn would be an estimate, so I'm not giving a figure.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

I can't answer this with the governed metrics. They have no campaign dimension. The only breakdowns are channel, channel group, marketing role, paid or unpaid, region and sales area. I can report cost per lead for Meta as a whole in 2024, but I can't split it by campaign or say which campaign was best.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

I can't answer this from the governed metrics. None of them covers gross margin, and there are no cost-of-goods or cost metrics other than paid media spend. Closed-won revenue is first-year contract value, so I can't work out margin from it. Estimating a margin would need a definition I don't have.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

I can't answer this with the governed metrics. Closed-won deals can be broken out by channel, channel group, marketing role, paid or unpaid, region and sales area. None of those dimensions covers fleet size, so I can't filter deals to fleets with more than 100 vehicles. The only fleet-related metric is the fleet activity index, which is a market-demand signal and doesn't describe individual customers. I won't estimate the number.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

I can't answer this with the governed metrics. None of them measures customer lifetime value. The closest are first-year contract value (`closed_won_revenue`) and average deal size. Both cover only the first year, so they leave out renewals, expansion, churn and retention. Calling either one lifetime value would be an estimate, and I don't have a definition for it.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

Fernhook's data has no TikTok channel, so I can't give a TikTok CPA for 2025. The nine paid channels are LinkedIn, Paid Search Brand, Paid Search Non-Brand, Meta, Connected TV, YouTube, Affiliates and Partners, Display Retargeting, and Webinars. A query filtered to TikTok returned no rows. I haven't estimated the figure or mapped TikTok onto another channel, such as Meta or YouTube.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}
